findings.location: architecture/w02-notes-errata/README.md PERF-032-F F15 bullet ('Not excluded: ... and a change outside the jsonschema family (such as a patched builtin) that leaves every corpus answer unchanged') and Round-3 dispositions row C3-1 ('is stated exactly'); scripts/perf032_followup.py module docstring F15 item ('Not excluded: ...'), _oracle_state and check_unique_oracle
findings.finding: The F15 'Not excluded' list is still not exhaustive. Three changes, each made by the exec, return 773 and are not in it (probes in /private/tmp/claude-501/cleanup-review-r4/probes/f15r4.py, one fresh process each). (1) State of a non-function object in the family: appending '_tc = jsonschema.Draft202012Validator.TYPE_CHECKER; object.__setattr__(_tc, "_type_checkers", _tc._type_checkers.insert("array", lambda checker, instance: False))' is accepted. Afterwards stock Draft202012Validator({'uniqueItems': True}).is_valid([1, 1]) is True, and [1, 1] is a corpus input. The snapshot compares only the identity of TYPE_CHECKER, which does not change. The post-corpus check calls _keywords.uniq directly and so never reaches validator.is_type. This change is inside the family and changes stock uniqueItems on a corpus input, so it matches neither listed exclusion. A variant that changes only arrays of 40 or more items (the corpus maximum is 32) is accepted too. (2) The family is read through sys.modules: the probe replaces sys.modules['jsonschema._utils'] and ['jsonschema._keywords'] with clone modules that hold the old values. It then rebinds the real _utils.uniq and _keywords.uniq to a rebuilt uniq that is wrong only for duplicate ints >= 5. This is accepted, and stock uniqueItems then accepts [5, 5]. That is the '_keywords.uniq ... rebinding' that the README lists as refused. (3) The check calls builtins at check time: the same rebinding, hidden by 'builtins.id = lambda o: old_id if o is new else real_id(o)', is accepted with the same effect. (3), and arguably (2), fall under 'a change outside the jsonschema family', but the stated item says only that such a change can 'leave every corpus answer unchanged', not that it can hide an in-family rebinding of uniq that the README says is refused. Every claim of what the snapshot covers ('by identity', function internals, kept alive) is literally true. The merged byte pin of the reviewed bytes still refuses all three, so the pipeline is not affected. The finding is about the stated limit, which the owner rule requires to be exact.
findings.requiredChange: State the residual exactly in the README F15 bullet, the module docstring and the C3-1 disposition. For example: 'Not excluded: a change triggered by anything other than the exec and the corpus calls; a change to the state of an object in the family other than the dicts and function internals listed (such as the Draft 2020-12 TYPE_CHECKER's attributes), unless it changes a unique or uniq answer on the corpus; and a change outside the family (builtins, sys.modules, standard-library modules) that leaves every corpus answer unchanged, including one that hides a change in the family from the snapshot.' Optional tightening, tested only as a probe idea and not as a fix: record id(sys.modules[name]) for each family module (kept alive), and after the corpus also require stock Draft202012Validator({'uniqueItems': True}).is_valid(case) to equal not-duplicate for each corpus case. These narrow (1) on corpus inputs and close the sys.modules swap, but they do not remove the need to state the residual.

findings.finding: Matching by final name does not see an alias bound in setup. In tests/test_selinux_matrix.py, 'm = map' followed by 'lazy = m(profile.historical_bytes, [path], [raw]) if route == "old_bytes" else None' passes check_route_test (25 calls). So does 'b = os.builtins.map' followed by 'b(...)', and so does an unlisted deferring callable such as itertools.islice. The literal wording ('a call whose final name is map ...') and the closed-list caveat cover all three. The merged validate_route_locality refuses both aliases ('route-local setup m'/'b') but accepts islice.
findings.requiredChange: None required. Optionally, refuse a setup value that is a bare Name or Attribute naming a listed callable, or say in the closed-list caveat that an alias bound in setup is not followed.
